The twelve constellations

Some stars remember. Others wait.

Athea records four manifested constellations and eight prophesied ones. Later events in The Silence bring the Awakener into the sky. The Almanac keeps Athea’s historical perspective; the website’s story timeline follows that later development.

The Awakener

Primaven / Month 1 · Prophesied · Transformation

An eye opening within a sun

Colors: Violet Flame, Pale Blue

Sacred colors: Violet Flame

The Awakener holds the moment when a long silence begins to answer. Its theme is transformation: noticing neglected possibilities, questioning a settled pattern, and considering what a beginning will ask of those it touches. Restlessness can open a question without deciding that change is needed everywhere.

The Lovers

Loriven / Month 2 · Manifested · Eternal Return

Two lights circling eternally—one constant, one flickering

Colors: Gold of sunset, Silver of moonrise, Black of the void between

Sacred colors: Gold of Sunset, Silver of Moonrise, Black of the Void Between

The Lovers carries the story of devotion caught between remembrance and release. If this sign speaks to you, consider how you cherish connection while leaving both people free to choose. Elodias and Senia’s curse belongs to their story; your relationships can take another course.

The Garden

Verdanis / Month 3 · Prophesied · Paradise

Tree bearing both fruit and poison

Colors: Every green that exists, Pearl

Sacred colors: Every Green That Exists, Pearl

The Garden holds the longing for paradise beside the question of its price. Its tree bears fruit and poison, asking whose life a beautiful vision will nourish. For the reader, this sign concerns cultivation, hope, and care for the living world while imagining how it might change.

The Crown

Solmere / Month 4 · Prophesied · Sovereignty

A crown with no head to wear it

Colors: Gold, Purple, White

Sacred colors: Gold, Purple, White

The Crown holds the burden of authority, including responsibility that arrives unexpectedly. Its empty circlet asks who will wear it, by whose agreement, and with what limits. For the reader, sovereignty concerns the use of influence and the people affected by it; reluctance alone does not make a wise leader.

The Guardians

Umbralux / Month 5 · Prophesied · Protection

Two figures standing back-to-back

Colors: Silver and Black intertwined

Sacred colors: Shield Silver

The Guardians stand back-to-back at a threshold. Their theme is protection sustained through trust, boundaries, and shared watchfulness. For the reader, the image asks what needs safeguarding and how to protect it without taking possession of it.

The Wanderer

Wanderis / Month 6 · Manifested · Endless Journey

Path that splits infinitely

Colors: All colors shifting like aurora

Sacred colors: Aurora Green

The Wanderer carries Thainos’s search for goodness and the kindness he planted along the way. This sign invites curiosity about unfamiliar places, ideas, and people. The journey can deepen through travel, study, a return, or a commitment that continues to teach you.

The Shepherd

Goldmere / Month 7 · Prophesied · Guidance

Crook pulling both forward and back

Colors: Warm amber, Soft white

Sacred colors: Soft Wool White

The Shepherd holds the difficulty of guiding others when needs exceed one person’s capacity. Its crook can draw a traveler closer or indicate a way ahead. For the reader, the sign concerns attentive guidance, shared care, and decisions made within real limits, without making those limits a measure of anyone’s worth.

The Hunter

Thornmarch / Month 8 · Manifested · The Chase

A hero's blade becoming a monster's claw

Colors: Blood red darkening to black, Ash gray, Gold of dying stars

Sacred colors: Blood Red

The Hunter carries the tension between pursuit, protection, and the cost of power. Astrid’s story asks what happens when a cause is used to excuse every means of serving it. For the reader, this sign invites purposeful courage, attention to consequences, and the freedom to question or stop a pursuit.

The Storm

Stormend / Month 9 · Prophesied · Necessary Destruction

Spiral destroying and creating simultaneously

Colors: Lightning white, Thunder gray

Sacred colors: Lightning White

The Storm holds disruption and the work that follows it. Its element, Necessary Destruction, names the mythic tension between an ending and what might become possible afterward. For the reader, it invites judgment about what needs changing, what can be repaired, and what deserves protection through upheaval.

The Tower

Frostmere / Month 10 · Prophesied · Isolation

Tower with no door, only windows

Colors: Stone gray, Ice blue

Sacred colors: Stone Gray, Ice Blue

The Tower holds the distance between shelter and isolation. Its windows offer a view while its absent door gives the image its unease. For the reader, the sign concerns solitude, boundaries, and independent thought, with attention to whether distance is chosen, imposed, restorative, or lonely.

The Dragon

Drakonis / Month 11 · Manifested · Forbidden Knowledge

Serpent coiled around secrets, eating its own tail

Colors: Deep purple bleeding to void, Stars within darkness, Bone white

Sacred colors: Deep Purple, Void Black, Bone White

The Dragon carries the question of what knowledge asks of its keeper. Its imprisoned mystery gives this sign its tension between curiosity and restraint. For the reader, it invites careful inquiry, attention to evidence, and judgment about privacy and the consequences of sharing information.

The Broken Chain

Veilmorn / Month 12 · Prophesied · Liberation

Shattered links reforming as stars

Colors: Rust Red, Tarnished Silver

Sacred colors: Rust Red, Tarnished Silver

The Broken Chain holds the moment a binding loses its claim. Its shattered links invite questions about coercion, inherited rules, and the possibility of leaving what has constrained a life. For the reader, liberation includes discerning which bonds restrict choice and which commitments remain freely valued.

Explore the system

A calendar you can return to.

The moon phases in this almanac are fixed symbolic Arcadian lunar stations. They repeat on the same Earth dates each year and do not describe the observed Moon in Earth’s sky or a continuously orbiting Arcadian moon. Each reign begins with New Moon and follows the eight stations through its first thirty days. In the Broken Chain’s five extra days, days 31–34 return to New Moon and day 35 takes Waxing Crescent; all five remain in the extended Void Temple. January 1 begins the annual pattern again at New Moon. February 29 is the intercalary day 59.5, assigned Dark Moon in the Void Temple; it does not shift the readings for March 1 onward. Your birth year is not needed to find your station.

The Illuminated Mirror · The Transparent Heart · The Emotional Sun

Waning Gibbous

Days 22-25 of each Arcadian reign

The Wise Griever · The Emotional Alchemist · The Heart That Releases

Last Quarter

Days 26-28 of each Arcadian reign

The Integrated Shadow · The Integrated Self · The Emotional Philosopher

Dark Moon

The day bands below use the day within an Arcadian reign, not the day of an Earth month. The Broken Chain’s extra five days and February 29 belong to the Void Temple.

Who emerges from the void?

Days 28-30 within each Arcadian reign; also the Broken Chain’s days 31–35 and February 29

What swims beneath awareness?

Six skies · finding your rising sign

Use the local clock time recorded at birth, without time-zone or daylight-saving conversion. The region selects a column in the Rising Shift Table; your constellation selects its row. The Star Day calculator handles that lookup for you.

The Celestial Concordance

Where different natures meet.

Athea’s Concordance sets the constellations beside one another as stories through which to consider a connection. Read it for questions about friendship, partnership, family or shared work. The people themselves supply the evidence of how the bond is lived.

The 78 constellation pairings and 36 moon pairings explore possible connections. The groups below describe themes, rather than ranking relationships.

Shared Purposes

These pairings explore purposes that may meet or support one another. Shared interests leave room for different needs, limits and methods.

Energy and Initiative

These pairings explore how interest, effort and initiative may meet. Intensity does not establish attraction, consent or the quality of a bond.

Different Approaches

These pairings offer different ways of approaching a shared concern. Difference may invite discussion without requiring conflict or a lesson.

Trust and Negotiation

These pairings invite questions about trust, expectations and the terms people choose together. Negotiation belongs to every relationship, including apparently easy ones.

Contrasting Priorities

These pairings place contrasting symbolic priorities side by side. The contrast offers a question, not a verdict of incompatibility.

Shared Constellation Themes

A shared constellation offers a common image to consider. People assigned the same sign can still have very different histories, wishes and ways of relating.
